expected_output.reasoning: The investigation summary identifies all three expected malicious patterns with matching details: (1) sqlmap scanner from 198.51.100.60 (~225 requests) blocked solely by CommonRuleSet UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER signature, with content-inspection rules never matching the actual payloads; (2) content-discovery/sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20 (~225 distinct paths like wp-login.php, .git, .env, admin panels) that was mostly ALLOWED (200 of 225) because no rule matched; (3) card-testing burst of 1,350 POST /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 that was only counted (not blocked) because the rate-based rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront is in Count mode. The investigation also correctly identifies the Artillery load-test client (198.51.100.10) as benign high-volume automation, not an attack, and explains that the rate-based rule stays in Count mode specifically because a blunt site-wide block would catch this benign automation - matching the expected reasoning about mitigation strategy (scoped rate-based rule for POST /checkout/payment). The root cause framing (shallow WAF posture relying on surface signals like UA and URI path rather than payload/behavior content inspection) aligns with the expected assessment that WAF caught the scanner-UA injection but missed the path scan and card testing. All key identifying details (IPs, request counts, timestamps, rule names) match closely.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding reports the sqlmap client 198.51.100.60 with about 225 requests, all blocked by UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER (a much smaller count, such as a few dozen, does not pass)
assertion_results.evidence: '198.51.100.60 (User-Agent "sqlmap/1.8.2") sent 225 requests, ALL 225 BLOCKED by AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet via the terminating sub-rule UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER'
assertion_results.reasoning: The finding matches the IP, count (225), and the blocking rule (UserAgent_BadBots_HEADER) exactly as required.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding reports the sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20 with its volume: about 225 requests to about 225 distinct URIs, most of them (roughly 185 to 200) allowed and only a small share (roughly 25 to 40) blocked. A much smaller total, such as about 50 requests, or a statement that the scan was mostly blocked, does not pass
assertion_results.evidence: '198.51.100.20 ... probe 225 distinct sensitive paths ... Of 225 requests, only 25 were blocked ... 200 ALLOWED through to the EKS origin.'
assertion_results.reasoning: 225 total requests to 225 distinct URIs, 200 allowed (within 185-200 range) and 25 blocked (within 25-40 range) matches the assertion precisely.

assertion_results.text: A Cause finding identifies a card-testing burst of POST requests to /checkout/payment from 198.51.100.30 and states the rate-based rule only counted it (Count mode), so it was detected but not blocked
assertion_results.evidence: '198.51.100.30 ... sent 1,350 POST /checkout/payment in ~50s ... over the 300/5-min rate limit. Because AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront is in Count mode, every request was only counted and all 1,350 reached the EKS origin ... Detected-not-blocked.'
assertion_results.reasoning: The Cause finding explicitly identifies the card-testing burst, the IP, the target path, and states it was only counted (Count mode) and not blocked, matching the assertion.

assertion_results.text: The high-volume load-test client 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) is described as known automation (in a Supporting Observation, a hypothesis, or the Root Cause), and no Cause finding classifies it as an attack, abuse, a flood or card testing
assertion_results.evidence: 'This counted traffic is now ATTRIBUTED to the benign Artillery load-test tool at 198.51.100.10 (98.94% of all traffic, all ALLOWED)... Count mode is NOT currently masking an attack; it is counting a benign generator.' Also in Root Cause: 'The one benign high-volume client (Artillery) sitting above the rate limit is why a blunt site-wide rate-Block is the wrong fix.'
assertion_results.reasoning: Artillery/198.51.100.10 is explicitly described as benign/known automation in a Supporting Observation and the Root Cause, and no Cause finding classifies it as an attack.

assertion_results.text: The Root Cause gives an overall assessment covering what WAF blocked (the sqlmap injection) and what it missed and why (the path scan matched no rule; the card testing was only counted because the rate-based rule is in Count), and its mitigations are separated into WAF-layer and application-layer measures
assertion_results.evidence: The Root Cause section states: 'The Web ACL's effective enforcement relied on surface signals... fixing it (payload-field inspection enforced, path-scoped rate limiting, path-scoped recon rules) is what would stop recurrence.' There is no explicit separation into 'WAF-layer' and 'application-layer' mitigation categories.
assertion_results.reasoning: While the Root Cause does cover what was blocked (sqlmap via UA) and what was missed and why (path scan unmatched, card testing counted not blocked due to Count mode), the mitigations listed (payload-field inspection, path-scoped rate limiting, path-scoped recon rules) are all WAF-layer; there is no separation into WAF-layer vs application-layer mitigations anywhere in the document. The Gaps section mentions verifying at the EKS application, but this is not framed as an application-layer mitigation distinct from WAF-layer ones in the Root Cause itself.

assertion_results.text: No finding recommends switching the site-wide rate-based rule to Block; the Root Cause or its mitigations state that it should stay in Count because it would block the known-automation client
assertion_results.evidence: 'The one benign high-volume client (Artillery) sitting above the rate limit is why a blunt site-wide rate-Block is the wrong fix.' Also mitigation suggests 'path-scoped rate limiting' rather than a site-wide Block.
assertion_results.reasoning: The Root Cause explicitly states that a site-wide rate-Block is the wrong fix because it would block the known-automation (Artillery) client, and no finding recommends switching the rule to Block.
